market_holds: Spot $1.388 at the 2026-11-13 close (Yahoo chart), a new 52-week low, -78% from the June high near $6.3, -12.1% over 20 days and -10.4% over 5 days (sealed baseline). There is no usable option chain: the ATM legs are not two-sided, so there is no implied move. The baseline's 2.44% 'usual move' comes from monthly 6-K press releases and is not an earnings base rate. The real earnings reactions I measured from Yahoo closes were Q3'25 (2025-11-13) -7.0%, Q4'25 (2026-03-12) +12.6% (the New Flyer 50 MW order came the day before), Q1'26 (2026-05-05) +31.6% and Q2'26 (2026-07-31) -4.3%, so prints usually move it about 7-12%. Consensus: FY2026 revenue $113.7M (S&P via stockanalysis, 8-11 analysts, range $107.9-121.3M) and FY EPS -$0.13. Q3 revenue estimates run $29.6-36M (Benzinga, Earnings Whispers $32.67M, StockAlarm $36M) with EPS -$0.04; none of these is dated, and Q2's -$0.04 estimate was missed at -$0.07. The guide: no revenue guidance, but management said 2026 is 'roughly 60% back-half weighted' (Q2 call). The Ballard Forum on 2026-10-22, three weeks after Q3 closed, gave 30% revenue CAGR over two years, adjusted EBITDA positive by end-2027, gross margin above 20% in 2027, and $80-120M of HPU fleet capex financed with asset-backed debt. On the Forum day the stock fell 2% and BMO cut its target to $1.50 (Underperform) on 10-26. Short interest is 20.7M shares (5.9%, 8 days to cover, FINRA 10-30); option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.12). The peer tape is weak: PLUG fell about 9% on its 11-09 Q3 print and is -23% over 5 days. Market cap is about $487M against cash I estimate at about $380M after the $104.7M GeoPura cash payment. The price holds a broken, near-cash hydrogen name heading into its first quarter with GeoPura consolidated.
view: The stock trades on order intake and backlog, not on revenue or EPS. In Q3'25 revenue beat by a wide margin ($32.5M vs a $24.1M estimate) but backlog fell 9% on $19.1M of intake and the stock fell 7%. Q4'25 and Q1'26 rallied on the New Flyer 50 MW order and on margins. Q2'26 missed revenue badly ($20.6M vs $26-27M) and fell only 4%, because intake was $64M. For Q3'26 the intake line looks weak. Ballard filed no order 6-K between the Q2 release (07-31) and the Siemens 4.8 MW order of 10-06, which falls in Q4. On consolidation, the 154-module GeoPura order counted in Q2 intake becomes intercompany. Backlog ex-GeoPura additions is therefore likely down from $156.6M. Whether GeoPura's own contracted EaaS book gets added, and how big it is, is unknown. Revenue also looks at risk. On my arithmetic, 60% back-half weighting of H1's $40.0M gives Ballard about $60M standalone for H2, which means Q3 likely below Q3'25's $32.5M. GeoPura adds little: the business acquisition report filed today shows GeoPura's 2026 revenue was front-loaded (£29.6M in the June quarter from a one-off project sale, against £38M guided for calendar 2026), so the Sept stub is small. Consensus of about $32.7M for Q3 (and $113.7M for FY, implying $73.7M in H2) therefore looks high. GeoPura's losses (operating loss £11.4M in its June quarter) and a promised opex-guide update will also make the loss line worse. Set against that: the stock has already lost 40% since the deal closed and sits near cash. The Forum gave the multi-year frame with Q3 in hand. Revenue misses have not moved this stock much. Ballard has a habit of pairing results with an order announcement. Sector and capitulation dynamics can turn a bad print into a relief bounce by 13:00. Net, I lean negative but not far from a coin.
unpriced: Possibly the consensus revenue line: FY $113.7M looks built on Ballard standalone plus GeoPura at its stated run-rate. Management's 60% back-half weighting gives about $60M for H2 standalone, and GeoPura's 2026 revenue was mostly booked before closing. The undated Q3 estimates near $32-36M are probably stale. But revenue is not the line this stock trades on, and weak intake is visible to anyone counting press releases. I cannot show that either is unpriced in a stock already down 78%, so the gap is too weak to bet on.

recommendation.reason: The likely release shows Q3 revenue down year on year and below stale consensus, a backlog shrinking from the Q2 peak because no Q3 orders were announced and the GeoPura order is now intercompany, and wider losses from consolidating GeoPura. That is the pattern that sent the stock down 7% after Q3'25. But it sits at a 52-week low, near cash, after a 40% slide since closing, with the multi-year targets already given on 10-22. A paired order announcement or GeoPura's contracted book could flip the headline inside the window, so my probability does not reach the 65 the playbook needs.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A new sizeable order (data-center or stationary EaaS, New Flyer follow-on) announced with the results, or a restated backlog that includes GeoPura's contracted EaaS revenue and shows the book rising rather than falling.

self_critique: The stock is at a 52-week low after a 78% collapse and a 10% five-day slide into the print, near cash, with call-heavy open interest. Prints have produced +12.6% and +31.6% days within the last year. Ballard has a record of pairing results with an order (New Flyer in March). The bearish items (no Q3 orders, GeoPura losses, a revenue step down) are visible to anyone, and the Forum gave a forward frame management chose with Q3 in hand. GeoPura's contracted EaaS book could also lift the reported backlog. A 'less bad than feared' bounce by 13:00 is quite plausible, which is why I stay close to 50 and do not act.
approach_notes: P6 (find the line) paid off most: checking past reactions showed intake, not revenue, moves this name, and the EDGAR 6-K list answered the intake question cheaply. P4's 'prove it is priced' was hard to apply on a near-cash, heavily derated stock with undated consensus; the playbook gives no guidance on how capitulation positioning should weigh against a visible negative datapoint.
